title: Cobalt Finance - cascading timeout postmortem and ops realignment
next_steps: Redwood SE to share detailed kernel-and-runtime timeline logs (by 2027-10-10)
Cobalt to run isolated e2e replay and share condensed packet capture (by 2027-10-12)
Schedule 1:1 runbook walk-through with Cobalt ops team (2027-10-14)
Redwood to propose fallback policy adjustments and a canary plan for production (by 2027-10-13)
action_items: Daniel Brooks - Extract kernel selection trace for the incident window - 2027-10-10
Sofia Martinez - Provide traffic shaping and autoscaler config from the cluster - 2027-10-11
Priya Nair - Share SOC2/PCI scoping doc and audit contact - 2027-10-09
Liam O'Connor - Run KV cache consistency check and forward results - 2027-10-12
summary: Postmortem review of cascade timeouts affecting Cobalt Finance's Private deployment. Root cause appears to be combined effects of a KV cache eviction storm, oversized batching during a traffic spike, and a kernel fallback path that increased p95 latency. Agreed immediate mitigations and runway for sustained fixes; plan for runbook updates and a controlled canary rollout.
topics: KV cache behavior and eviction policy
Kernel fallback and quantization path performance
Compliance and audit artifacts to share
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. We're gonna run through the incident timeline and make sure next steps are clear. we have Daniel and Priya from Redwood. how's everyone over there at Cobalt?

[00:18] Ethan Park: Hi Maria, thanks. We're okay, it's been a rough week. We had production slowdowns that cascaded through payments and risk checks. we'll need a clear path to mitigate and prevent.

[00:34] Sofia Martinez: Thanks. we opened this to also talk about runbook alignment — our oncall folks hit several manual toggles that we wanna automate.

[00:45] Daniel Brooks: quick context from our side — we looked at the traces you shared and saw a cluster of requests that triggered a large KV cache eviction followed by a number of model kernel fallbacks. when eviction happened, a lot of prefix cache misses produced higher compute per request and the batching subsystem attempted to increase batch sizes to preserve throughput which paradoxically spiked latency.

[01:11] Liam O'Connor: that matches our metrics. p50 stayed fine but p95 and p99 blew out. the payments flow has tight 200ms SLAs; anything over that started tripping internal timeouts and retries.

[01:28] Maria Chen: sorry interject — can you describe "kernel fallback" for the folks on the call? i've seen it mentioned in the engineering notes.

[01:36] Daniel Brooks: sure, so the runtime picks a fast optimized kernel for the active model when memory and sequence lengths fit the fast path. under memory pressure or certain sequence-length combos we roll to a more generic kernel that's slower but more compatible. in this incident a lot of requests moved to the generic kernel which increased token compute time by ~3x in the traces we saw.

[02:02] Ethan Park: do we know what triggered the kernel switch? was it quantization mismatch or memory?

[02:09] Daniel Brooks: primarily memory pressure and also some outliers in sequence length because of a spike in batched requests. the eviction storm meant that the KV cache couldn't be used for prefixes and so effective sequence work grew.

[02:24] Sofia Martinez: to be clear — this was a private deployment in our VPC with Redwood Private, right? We had dedicated nodes and the autoscaler should have handled this.

[02:33] Priya Nair: correct, this is Redwood Private on your dedicated pool. autoscaling was active, but the autoscaler scaling step was tuned to avoid noisy scaling; the initial knobs slowed reactive scaling. we recommended those conservative values due to cost constraints previously.

[02:51] Liam O'Connor: and we'd recently tightened cost controls — so yes, conservative autoscaler. hindsight, that was part of the problem.

[03:00] Ethan Park: can you walk us through the timeline starting from 09:14 UTC? our SRE doc has a rough window.

[03:08] Daniel Brooks: yes. at 09:14 we observed a sudden 3x increase in requests that hit the model endpoint — looks like a backfill job from your analytics cluster. at 09:16 KV cache eviction rate spikes; by 09:19 batch controller increases target batch size to keep throughput; at 09:21 multiple kernels report mismatch and fall back; by 09:23 p95 latency crosses your 200ms alarm; at 09:28 retries and downstream cascading timeouts occur.

[03:39] Sofia Martinez: the backfill was scheduled by internal billing reconciliation — it shouldn't have hit the online path. there's a config gap; we'll address that.

[03:48] Maria Chen: okay so we have three contributing factors: traffic misrouting/backfill, KV cache eviction behavior, and conservative autoscaler plus batching interactions. any other drivers?

[03:59] Daniel Brooks: small one — we saw intermittent NIC drops on one host for about 30s which intensified the pressure on remaining nodes. not the cause but an amplifier.

[04:12] Nadia Rahman: from compliance — were any PII logging misexposed during retries or dumps? we opened a ticket to check.

[04:21] Priya Nair: initial check shows no raw payload leaks; retries were at the request routing layer. we'll deliver a sanitized log bundle for your review.

[04:33] Ethan Park: thanks. i want to focus on mitigations that we can do in the next 72 hours first. what are the low-risk fast wins?

[04:42] Daniel Brooks: fast wins: 1) add a short-lived emergency rule to throttle or queue the backfill source to avoid hitting online; 2) lower the max batch size cap during high latency windows to prioritize p95; 3) temporary raise autoscaler aggressiveness for a short window while we stabilize. we can propose exact knobs.

[05:05] Sofia Martinez: are those knobs safe from a compliance perspective? e.g., do throttles alter audit trails?

[05:12] Priya Nair: they don't alter content, only admission rates. we'll ensure audit logs still capture the throttling events for RCA.

[05:20] Liam O'Connor: can you also add a KV cache throttling or protective eviction policy? like pause big evictions.

[05:27] Daniel Brooks: yes — we can patch the eviction policy to be smoothing-aware so it doesn't evict the hot prefixes all at once. that'll be a medium-weight change but deployable to your private plane within a day if you approve.

[05:41] Ethan Park: what about the kernel fallback? if that path is 3x slower, can we short-circuit to an alternate model variant that has stable latency?

[05:50] Daniel Brooks: good question — we can do two things: one, bias the routing toward a smaller, faster variant under memory pressure; two, pre-warm the generic kernel by maintaining a lightweight dummy workload to keep caches warm. both have tradeoffs (cost for pre-warm, small quality delta for smaller variant).

[06:12] Sofia Martinez: hmm smaller variant may change output distribution — risk for fraud checks. we have to validate.

[06:19] Maria Chen: this is where evals help — we can run a quick quality regression on a representative sample before switching routing. Daniel, can your team run a regression test?

[06:29] Daniel Brooks: yes, we'll run a quick A/B on a 10k-sample prompt set and share delta metrics within 48 hours.

[06:36] Ethan Park: great. on the operational side we also want a clearer runbook: what to do when p95 spikes beyond threshold. currently our oncall toggled three switches and then manual failover — took 18 minutes.

[06:48] Priya Nair: agreed. we'll co-author a runbook v2 with explicit play actions: immediate throttle source, lower batch cap, enable aggressive scaling, and if still bad, route to the smaller variant. we'll include rollback steps.

[07:01] Liam O'Connor: i want the playbook steps to be automatable — we use Terraform for infra toggles where possible. can Redwood expose an API to flip the batch cap and routing policies?

[07:12] Daniel Brooks: yes, Redwood Private has an ops API; we'll share endpoint swagger and a small terraform provider snippet. Daniel to action.

[07:22] Sofia Martinez: we'll need RBAC checks too — we don't want devs toggling this accidentally.

[07:28] Maria Chen: noted — include RBAC in the runbook and terraform examples. Priya, can you own drafting and coordinating?

[07:34] Priya Nair: yes, I'll own runbook drafting and we'll iterate with Cobalt.

[07:40] Ethan Park: moving to long-term fixes — what does Redwood recommend architecturally?

[07:46] Daniel Brooks: long term: 1) smarter KV cache eviction (smoothing + TTL heuristics), 2) adaptive batching that reduces batch depth when per-request latency increases, 3) better kernel warm-up heuristics, 4) tag traffic sources and enforce path separation for heavy offline jobs.

[08:04] Nadia Rahman: on the tagging idea — we need logs to show separation for audits. will Redwood produce trace-level artifacts that map to our internal job IDs?

[08:13] Daniel Brooks: yes — we can enhance trace metadata to include customer-supplied tags (job-id, team, environment). we'll add that as a feature request and propose a short timeline.

[08:24] Sofia Martinez: timeline please — our compliance team needs evidence in Q4.

[08:28] Maria Chen: Daniel, can you propose delivery dates for the smoothing eviction and tagging feature?

[08:33] Daniel Brooks: we'll scope it this week; provisional plan: eviction smoothing in 3 weeks, tagging and trace metadata within 2 weeks as a smaller change.

[08:43] Ethan Park: good. now a couple nitty gritty questions from SRE: 

[08:47] Liam O'Connor: 1) the NIC flaps you mentioned — can you share host-level logs and whether the runtime retried connections or reaped sessions?

[08:55] Daniel Brooks: yes, we'll include the host NIC logs and a summary of connection handling. runtime retries were bounded but amplified load on neighbors.

[09:04] Liam O'Connor: 2) can you confirm that the KV cache uses client-specified keys only? we had concerns about prefix collision with another team.

[09:12] Daniel Brooks: KV cache is namespaced per-customer and per-model; collisions are unlikely but we'll audit the keys during the window to confirm.

[09:20] Sofia Martinez: there was also an ask earlier about failure-mode observability — when the kernel falls back can we bubble a distinct metric and alert?

[09:29] Priya Nair: absolutely. we can add a "kernel_fallback_rate" metric to your dashboard and wire an alert when it rises above baseline.

[09:37] Ethan Park: excellent. okay let's capture the immediate mitigation plan and owners.

[09:42] Maria Chen: recap: Daniel will extract kernel traces and host logs; Priya will draft runbook v2 and share RBAC/terraform snippets; Cobalt (Sofia/Liam) will run the isolated e2e replay and share traffic details; Redwood to run 10k eval on smaller model variant. deliverables with dates are in the next steps.

[10:01] Sofia Martinez: can we also get a quick cost estimate if we pre-warm kernels and increase autoscaler aggressiveness?

[10:08] Daniel Brooks: yes we'll provide a delta estimate — it's usually a predictable hourly bump depending on node hours. expect a small percentage but we'll quantify.

[10:18] Ethan Park: last question — how do we prevent backfill jobs from touching online traffic? we need policy suggestions not just knobs.

[10:25] Maria Chen: two-pronged: 1) tag and enforce path separation at the ingress (we'll help you set ingress policies), 2) recommend a job-scheduling rule that routes offline heavy jobs to batch-only endpoints. we'll provide a reference policy.

[10:40] Sofia Martinez: cool. are there any remaining concerns from the compliance side?

[10:44] Nadia Rahman: please include the scrubbed logs and a confirmation that no payment cards or PII were duplicated in dumps. we'll need a signed attestation.

[10:53] Priya Nair: we'll include sanitized logs and a short attestation draft for Nadia to review.

[11:00] Maria Chen: ok if there are no other blockers i'd like to lock the triage actions and cadence — we'll do a daily 20-minute stand for three days starting tomorrow to run progress and unblockers. is that acceptable?

[11:10] Ethan Park: yes, that works. we'll join the stand and assign our SRE to participate.

[11:16] Sofia Martinez: quick note — please send the runbook draft as a google doc we can comment on.

[11:21] Priya Nair: will do.

[11:24] Maria Chen: thank you all. we'll follow up with the log bundle and proposed knobs. any final comments?

[11:30] Liam O'Connor: just one — please mark the KA as priority in your tracking system so we can reference it in our ticketing.

[11:35] Daniel Brooks: done, i'll include the tracking id in the email.

[11:38] Maria Chen: perfect. end of call.

[52:00] -- meeting ended --
